item.title: Introducing our new Pravda network dataset: 15 million articles in 47 languages
item.description:
Our dataset on this pro-Kremlin Information Manipulation Set (IMS) has more than doubled: from over 7 million to more than 15 million articles, published across 88 websites in 47 languages. Here is what changed, what we share openly with the community, and what we make available to analysts who need to go further.

item.description:

item.title: #Disinfo2026: what we brought to Vilnius, and what others tried to take away
item.description:
CheckFirst took part in #Disinfo2026, speaking on FIMI infrastructure, covert influence campaigns and DSA vs climate disinformation. The conference opened under pressure: days earlier, three main sponsors had withdrawn their support after Washington reportedly objected to a panel examining the US as a FIMI threat.

The post #Disinfo2026: what we brought to Vilnius, and what others tried to take away appeared first on CheckFirst.

item.title: The Kremlin’s Digital Pirates: How Russian Tracking Pixels Harvest Romanians’ Data to Fund Conspiracies and Extremism
item.description:
For five months, we tracked over 100,000 ads displayed across 131 websites in Eastern Europe. After decoding the hidden mechanisms behind these ads, we uncovered a network of Russian companies. This investigation reveals what data is harvested from Romanians, who ends up receiving it, and why the ads shown on platforms with conspiratorial and extremist content are among the most valuable to this network.

The post The Kremlin’s Digital Pirates: How Russian Tracking Pixels Harvest Romanians’ Data to Fund Conspiracies and Extremism appeared first on CheckFirst.

item.title: Roska Bridge: How a pro-Russian IMS exploits vulnerabilities of decentralised platforms to spread propaganda
item.description:
Our new investigation reveals how a sophisticated Russian information manipulation set (IMS), dubbed “Roska Bridge”, uses alternative and decentralised social media platforms as a weapon to flood Western and domestic Russian audiences with aggressive, anti-Western, and anti-Ukrainian propaganda.
